additions.title: Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977, section 2: Negligence liability
additions.quote: In the case of other loss or damage, a person cannot so exclude or restrict his liability for negligence
additions.why: A binding limit on moving risk by contract. Liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence cannot be excluded at all; for other loss a term or notice excluding or restricting liability for negligence stands only so far as it is reasonable. It cuts both ways: it limits what an organisation can push on to others and what a supplier can disclaim. General contract law, not written for AI; s.2 does not apply to consumer contracts (Consumer Rights Act 2015 instead). England, Wales and Northern Ireland; Scotland has its own Part.

additions.title: SS2/21: Outsourcing and third party risk management (November 2024 update)
additions.publisher: Prudential Regulation Authority, Bank of England
additions.quote: Boards and senior management, in particular individuals performing SMFs, cannot outsource their responsibilities.
additions.why: A UK regulator's statement that sharing a risk with a supplier does not move accountability: the firm stays fully accountable for its regulatory obligations. The same chapter expects a documented exit plan for material arrangements. Applies to PRA-regulated banks, insurers and designated investment firms only; a supervisory statement, not a rule.

additions.title: UK Corporate Governance Code 2024
additions.quote: any material controls which have not operated effectively as at the balance sheet date, the action taken, or proposed, to improve them
additions.why: The code-level expectation that treatment is checked and reported, not only decided: the board reviews the effectiveness of risk management and internal control at least annually, declares whether material controls were effective, and describes those that were not and the action taken. Provision 28 asks how principal risks are being managed or mitigated. Applies on a comply-or-explain basis to listed companies; Provision 29 applies to accounting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2026. Not about AI specifically.

additions.title: Risk Management in the Artificial Intelligence Act
additions.publisher: European Journal of Risk Regulation (Cambridge University Press); author Jonas Schuett
additions.locator: Section V.2 'Risk management process, Article 9(2)', paragraph following Footnote 106
additions.quote: If it turns out that it is not possible to reduce residual risks to an acceptable level, the development and deployment process must be stopped.
additions.why: Peer-reviewed, open-access legal analysis of the EU risk management duty: assess, treat, reassess, and stop if residual risk cannot be made acceptable. Supports listing 'stop the activity' as a treatment option. Limits: it interprets the 2021 proposal and the 2022 Council text, not the Act as adopted and amended; it concerns providers of high-risk systems; doctrinal argument, not empirical evidence. EU law, not UK law.

additions.title: Insuring AI: The Role of Insurance in Artificial Intelligence Regulation
additions.publisher: Harvard Journal of Law & Technology, vol. 35 no. 2; author Anat Lior
additions.quote: Exceptions and exclusions can be silent rather than affirmative
additions.why: Research on insurance as a way of transferring AI risk. Argues insurance can channel safer behaviour, and sets out the drawbacks: moral hazard, difficulty pricing unfamiliar risks, and exclusions, including risks an insurer never foresaw and later writes out of standard policies. Supports the brief's caution that cover is uncertain. Limits: United States law and market; a law-review article (student-edited, not blind peer review); argument, not claims data; 2022.

additions.title: Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry: Report, Volume 1 (HC 1119)
additions.publisher: Post Office Horizon IT Inquiry (Sir Wyn Williams)
additions.quote: the Post Office maintained the fiction that its data was always accurate
additions.why: A statutory inquiry's finding on what happens when a known system risk is neither treated nor formally accepted: staff knew, or should have known, the system could produce false data, yet the organisation acted as if it could not. Limits: Horizon was an accounting system, not AI; Volume 1 deals with human impact and redress, and the inquiry's findings on governance and responsibility are for later volumes, not read here.

additions.title: Model Artificial Intelligence Governance Framework, Second Edition
additions.publisher: Infocomm Media Development Authority and Personal Data Protection Commission, Singapore
additions.quote: mitigate those risks, and maintain a response plan should mitigation fail
additions.why: International comparator. Singapore's voluntary framework treats risk treatment as continuing work: identify and review risks, mitigate them, keep a response plan in case mitigation fails, and record any departure from the organisation's own values as a conscious decision with a documented rationale. Voluntary; no legal force in the UK; predates generative AI.

One addition worth a line at the next version: the limits on sharing risk by contract are wider than the Equality Act (Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977 s.2 bars excluding liability for death or injury by negligence and subjects other exclusions to a reasonableness test).
